english_paragraphs: In 1941 George de Mestral, a Swiss engineer, returned from hunting in the Alps with his hound, an Irish Pointer. Prickly burdock seed-heads had hitched themselves to his clothes and lay tangled in the dog's fur. Under a microscope he saw thousands of tiny barbs, each a hook grasping the small loops in cloth.

Few took his idea seriously at first. In Lyon, then a weaving centre, a cotton version proved too frail to survive abrasion. Working with a textiles firm, he turned to nylon, whose hooks were stiff enough to hold yet easy to pull apart. The trial-and-error at the looms and mills lasted about ten years.

The name Velcro merged two French words, velours, meaning velvet, and crochet, meaning hook. A US patent duly followed in 1955. In 1959 a New York fashion show sent apparel stitched with the fasteners down the runway. The public was less charmed than expected, mostly because of the aesthetic.

The underdog proved its utility in outer space. NASA used it in the Apollo programme to keep gear anchored in weightlessness, so that nothing would hover in mid-air. Apollo 11 was equipped with a sizeable amount, about 3,300 square inches. NASA did not invent the nylon clasp.

When the patent ran out in 1978, cut-price knock-offs from other countries overran the market, and a niche product went mainstream. In 2017, to stop its brand-name melting into a generic noun, the company asked people to call such mimics hook and loop fasteners. In effect, the firm was asking the public to stop using its own name for rivals' goods.
chinese_source_paragraphs: 1941年，乔治·德·梅斯特拉尔，一位**瑞士的**(Swiss)工程师，带着他的**猎犬**(hound)，一只爱尔兰的指示犬，从阿尔卑斯山的打猎中归来。**多刺的**(Prickly)牛蒡**种子头**(seed-heads)已把它们自己**钩在了**(hitched)他的衣服上，并**缠绕**(tangled)在狗的**毛皮**(fur)里。在显微镜下，他看到成千上万个细小的**倒刺**(barbs)，每一个（如同）一个**钩子**(hook)，**抓住**(grasping)布料上的小**圈**(loops)。

起初，很少有人**认真看待**(took seriously)他的想法。在里昂，当时的一个**纺织**(weaving)中心，一个棉制版本被证明太**脆弱**(frail)，以至于无法在**磨损**(abrasion)中存活下来。与一家**纺织品**(textiles)公司合作，他转向了**尼龙**(nylon)，其钩子足够**坚硬且不易弯曲**(stiff)，既能扣住，又容易**拉开**(pull apart)。在**织机**(looms)旁和**工厂**(mills)里的**反复试验**(trial-and-error)持续了约十年。

Velcro 这个名字**合并了**(merged)两个法语词，velours 意为**天鹅绒**(velvet)，crochet 意为钩子。1955年，一项美国专利**如期**(duly)而至。1959年，纽约一场时装秀让**缝有**(stitched)这种**搭扣**(fasteners)的**服装**(apparel)走上**T台**(runway)。公众却不如预期那样**着迷**(charmed)，**主要**(mostly)是因为它的**审美**(aesthetic)。

这个**不被看好的（发明）**(underdog)在**外太空**(outer space)证明了自己的**用处**(utility)。美国航天局在**阿波罗计划**(Apollo programme)中使用了它，以便在**失重状态下**(in weightlessness)保持**装备**(gear)**固定**(anchored)，从而没有任何东西会在**半空**(mid-air)中**飘浮**(hover)。阿波罗11号**配备了**(equipped with)**相当多的**(sizeable)用量，约3,300平方英寸。美国航天局并没有发明这种尼龙**扣件**(clasp)。

1978年专利**到期**(ran out)后，来自其他国家的**廉价的**(cut-price)**仿制品/山寨品**(knock-offs)**泛滥于**(overran)市场，一种**小众**(niche)产品成了**主流**(mainstream)。2017年，为了阻止其**品牌名**(brand-name)逐渐**消融为**(melting into)一个**通用的**(generic)**名词**(noun)，该公司要求人们把这类**仿品**(mimics)称作为“钩毛搭扣”。**实际上**(in effect)，这家公司是在请求公众停止将其自己的名字用在**对手的**(rivals')商品上。

approved_summary: 瑞士工程师梅斯特拉尔发现刺果用微钩扣住衣物毛圈，便仿照它设计可反复扣合、拉开的搭扣。
棉制搭扣不耐磨，他改用尼龙，反复试验约十年，1955年获得美国专利。
公众主要因外观而反应冷淡；美国航天局在阿波罗计划中用搭扣固定失重中的装备，并非搭扣的发明者。
1978年专利到期后，廉价仿品涌入市场，原本小众的搭扣逐渐成为日常用品。
Velcro是品牌名；2017年品牌方要求将仿品称为钩毛搭扣，避免自家商标泛指整类产品。
